sources.title: Adobe: What Is Exposure in Photography?
sources.author: Adobe
sources.content: Photographic exposure is controlled through aperture, shutter speed, and ISO. Aperture changes the opening that admits light and also affects depth of field. Shutter speed controls how long light reaches the sensor and changes the appearance of motion. ISO changes the camera's sensitivity or signal amplification and can affect visible noise. The settings work together, so changing one may require compensation with another for a similar brightness.
